s: A 73 m red-sandstone victory tower begun around 1199, one of the tallest brick minarets in the world. Only spottable in the first minutes after take-off from Delhi, south-east of the airport.
l: A thin pale spike surrounded by green lawns and ruins in Mehrauli.

s: The Yamuna flows 1,376 km from the Himalayan Yamunotri glacier to meet the Ganges at Prayagraj. Through Delhi it is lined with wide floodplains and farms.
l: A broad sandy riverbed with a narrow channel, bridges every few kilometres.

s: The Aravallis are among the oldest fold mountains on Earth, roughly 1.5–2 billion years old. Around Delhi they are worn down to low rocky ridges and scrub forest, the last tip of a range that runs 670 km to Gujarat.
l: Brown, crumpled low hills breaking up the flat plain south of Delhi.

s: Dry deciduous forest in the Aravalli hills of Alwar district. Tigers vanished here by 2005 and were reintroduced from Ranthambore in 2008 — the first such relocation in India.
l: A darker patch of rugged, wooded hills west of Alwar.

s: Revered as the birthplace of Krishna, Mathura sits on the west bank of the Yamuna and has been a city for over 2,500 years.
l: A dense town hugging a bend of the Yamuna; the Mathura refinery's tanks lie just south.

s: Shah Jahan's white-marble mausoleum (completed c. 1653) stands on the south bank of the Yamuna in Agra, with Agra Fort 2.5 km upstream.
l: Look for the river's sharp bends through Agra. The Taj itself is small from cruise height — a white dot with a green garden square on the river bank.

s: A man-made wetland near Bharatpur, once a royal duck-shooting reserve and now a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for winter migratory birds.
l: Patchy shallow water and marsh in an otherwise farmed plain (wettest after the monsoon).

s: The Chambal has carved a maze of deep, eroded badlands along its banks — the ravines once hid the region's famous dacoits. The river itself is protected as the National Chambal Sanctuary for gharials and river dolphins.
l: A wide band of wrinkled, finger-like gullies either side of a winding river — very distinctive from the air.

s: A hill fort on a 3 km-long sandstone plateau rising about 100 m above the city of Gwalior, fortified since at least the 8th century.
l: A long, flat-topped rocky mesa in the middle of the city.

s: Forested plateau with two large lakes, Sakhya Sagar and Madhav Sagar, once the summer capital of Gwalior's Scindia rulers.
l: Dark forest with lakes next to the town of Shivpuri.

s: Jhansi is famous for Rani Lakshmibai's stand in 1857. Ten km away, Orchha's riverside palaces and cenotaphs line the Betwa.
l: Rocky granite outcrops of Bundelkhand and the Betwa river winding past.

s: The Great Stupa at Sanchi was commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE and is one of the oldest stone structures in India.
l: A small hilltop north of Vidisha — hard to spot; use Vidisha and the Betwa river as your guide.

s: Bhopal, the 'City of Lakes', grew around the Upper Lake, created by an earthen dam attributed to the 11th-century king Raja Bhoj. It still supplies much of the city's drinking water.
l: A large irregular lake on the west side of the city with the smaller Lower Lake beside it.

s: Sandstone shelters in the Vindhya foothills with rock paintings, some estimated at over 10,000 years old — a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
l: Forested Vindhyan ridges south of Bhopal; the shelters themselves are too small to see.

s: A broken chain of plateaus and escarpments traditionally seen as the boundary between North and South India.
l: Steep, forested escarpment edges stepping down towards the Narmada valley.

s: One of India's few major rivers flowing west, the Narmada runs 1,312 km in a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges to the Arabian Sea.
l: A wide river in a flat valley floor, with the town of Narmadapuram (Hoshangabad) on its south bank.

s: A large reservoir on the Tawa, a tributary of the Narmada, on the edge of Satpura National Park.
l: A big, many-armed lake in forested hills.

s: Pachmarhi is Madhya Pradesh's only hill station. Dhupgarh (1,350 m), the highest point of the Satpuras, rises nearby amid sandstone gorges and sal forest.
l: The darkest, most rugged forest you'll see in central India.

s: Part of the Satpura hills in northern Maharashtra and one of the first nine tiger reserves created under Project Tiger in 1973–74.
l: Deeply folded green hills north-west of Amravati.

s: A major city of Maharashtra's Vidarbha region, a centre of the cotton trade on the Deccan plain.
l: Flat black cotton-soil farmland around a compact city.

s: Close to India's geographic centre — the Zero Mile Stone here was the reference point for distances in British India. Famous for oranges.
l: Well off the route; at night its lights glow on the horizon.

s: Tributaries of the Godavari draining the Deccan basalts. The flat-topped hills around are layers of the Deccan Traps — lava flows about 66 million years old.
l: Stepped, flat-topped basalt hills and meandering rivers.

s: A large dam on the Godavari river near Nizamabad. The Godavari, at 1,465 km, is the second-longest river in India.
l: A huge sprawling lake on the Godavari — one of the best-defined landmarks on the Delhi–Hyderabad route.

s: The 15th-century capital of the Bahmani Sultanate, built on a red laterite plateau.
l: Red soil plateau with the old walled town on its edge.

s: A heart-shaped lake built in 1563, linking Hyderabad and Secunderabad, with a 16 m monolithic Buddha statue on an island.
l: Approaching Hyderabad: Hussain Sagar in the city centre, the twin reservoirs Osman Sagar and Himayat Sagar to the west, and the granite boulder hills all around.

s: A granite hill fortress, once the seat of the Qutb Shahi dynasty and the market for diamonds such as the Koh-i-Noor.
l: A rocky hill crowned with walls on Hyderabad's west side.

s: India's fourth-largest river, rising in the Western Ghats and flowing 1,400 km east to the Bay of Bengal.
l: A broad river, often braided with sandbars, crossing the dry Deccan.

s: A vast reservoir near Hosapete. Just downstream lie the boulder-strewn ruins of Hampi, capital of the Vijayanagara Empire.
l: A large lake, then a landscape of giant granite boulders.

s: Former capital of Andhra State (1953–56), at the confluence of the Tungabhadra and Hindri rivers.
l: City at the river junction; the Tungabhadra joins the Krishna just downstream.

s: One of the driest districts in South India, dotted with irrigation tanks and, increasingly, huge solar and wind parks.
l: Reddish dry plateau with scattered tanks (small reservoirs).

s: Home to the 16th-century Veerabhadra temple with its hanging pillar and a huge monolithic Nandi bull.
l: Small village near Hindupur — use it as a marker that Bengaluru is about 120 km ahead.

s: An ancient hill fortress 1,478 m high, just north of Bengaluru airport, and the source of several rivers.
l: A lone steep hill to the side as you descend into Bengaluru.

s: India's largest inland salt lake, a seasonal saline wetland whose salt works have operated for centuries. It hosts flamingos in winter.
l: A large pale or white flat west of Jaipur — salt pans with rectangular evaporation grids.

s: The Pink City, founded in 1727 by Sawai Jai Singh II on a grid plan. Amber Fort and Nahargarh guard the Aravalli ridges to its north.
l: A large city boxed in by Aravalli ridges, with Jal Mahal's lake on the Amber road.

s: A dam on the Banas river that supplies drinking water to Jaipur and Ajmer.
l: A long lake winding through gaps in the Aravalli ridges near Tonk.

s: Ajmer is home to the Sufi shrine of Moinuddin Chishti; just over the Nag Pahar ridge lies Pushkar, with its holy lake and camel fair.
l: A city around the Ana Sagar lake, ringed by Aravalli hills.

s: A small Rajput town famous for its stepwells and Taragarh Fort clinging to the Aravalli ridge.
l: A town tucked into a narrow ridge valley north-west of Kota.

s: Kota sits on the Chambal river, which is stepped by a chain of four dams: Gandhi Sagar, Rana Pratap Sagar, Jawahar Sagar and the Kota Barrage.
l: The river cutting through a city, with a chain of reservoirs upstream to the south.

s: Reservoir on the Chambal at Rawatbhata, next to the Rajasthan Atomic Power Station.
l: A long, branching lake in rocky country south of Kota.

s: Completed in 1960, the first and largest of the Chambal dams, its reservoir covers over 600 km².
l: A very large, irregular lake — one of the most obvious features on the Delhi–Mumbai route.

s: One of the largest forts in India, stretching about 3 km along a mesa 180 m above the plain — the site of three famous sieges.
l: A long, narrow flat-topped hill with walls along its rim.

s: The Mahi is one of the few rivers that crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice. Kadana Dam impounds it on the Gujarat–Rajasthan border.
l: A green, many-fingered reservoir in hilly tribal country.

s: At about 23.44°N, the northernmost latitude where the Sun can be directly overhead (at the June solstice). All four routes from Delhi cross it: near Bhopal and Sanchi going south, and over southern Rajasthan on the way to Mumbai.
l: Nothing to see on the ground, but it's a nice moment to note.

s: The Narmada widens into a broad tidal estuary at Bharuch, one of the oldest ports in India (ancient Barygaza), before reaching the Gulf of Khambhat.
l: A wide brown river mouth opening into the sea.

s: A funnel-shaped inlet of the Arabian Sea with some of the highest tidal ranges in India — up to about 11 m.
l: Silty brown water and wide mudflats along the coast.

s: Surat, on the Tapi, is one of the world's leading diamond-cutting centres and a historic Mughal-era port.
l: A big city on a meandering river close to the coast.

s: A UNESCO-listed mountain chain running 1,600 km parallel to the west coast, one of the world's biodiversity hotspots. Near Nashik it holds the source of the Godavari at Trimbakeshwar.
l: Steep forested escarpments and flat-topped hills rising inland from the coastal plain.

n: Mumbai: Powai, Sea Link & Marine Drive
s: Mumbai was built on seven islands joined by land reclamation. On approach, look for Powai Lake, the forested Sanjay Gandhi National Park, and the cable-stayed Bandra–Worli Sea Link.
l: Depending on the runway: the curve of Marine Drive (the 'Queen's Necklace' at night) and the Sea Link across Mahim Bay.
